gaps.what: Who held Greater Poland 1239-1242 is not settled by the pages: the Odonic page (main text) leaves Ujście and Nakło to Odonic and his sons, the Duchy of Greater Poland page and the Odonic footnote say Henry II controlled all of it; the dossier draws Ujście and Nakło only (the first report's 'page silent' entry for 1238-1239 was wrong: only the Henry I page is silent)

No page dates the loss of Wieluń (drawn 1249-1299; Wieluń page: 'in the second half of the 13th century, was in Duchy of Greater Poland', Land of Wieluń by 1299); Cliopatria draws the 9 cells under Sandomierz (1250-1278) and Duchies of Poland (1279-1304)

Who took Pomerelia in 1296 (Władysław I page silent; Pomerania subordinate to Władysław only at the end of 1306); who held Greater Poland 1305-1314 is in the dissolve note only (Henry III of Głogów 1305-1309 per the ruler table, Władysław I 1314 by 'Three years later' than 1311)
Wałcz cells (8): Cliopatria gives them to Brandenburg in 1272, the Margraviate of Brandenburg page in 1296; the dossier follows the page, so Brandenburg's 1272 gain overlaps it 1272-1295

Radom's return to Sandomierz in 1239 (c1, the page says only that Konrad renounced his claims over Sandomierz); Lithuanian strip of 1326 (the Wenceslaus of Płock page names no land); ruler strip 1313-1351; the one-to-seven-cell changes of 1250, 1279 and 1305

Łódź-Łęczyca remainder of the Greater Poland dossier's wider 1228 Seniorate (about 290 cells) has no holder 1229-1231; the Silesia dossier's 1232 Kraków gain names duchy-of-greater-poland instead of Konrad
The vassal duchy of 1351-1526 and the Rawa, Czersk and Płock duchies after 1313 are not drawn; identity.end 1351 follows Cliopatria

problems: Fixes applied (12): Greater Poland 7 (1239 loss to Silesia with keyframes; Kuyavia subtracted from the Seniorate events and keyframes; Kuyavia 1199 counterpart duchy-of-kuyavia; Wieluń drawn 1249-1299; keyframe 1244-1249 split at 1247 and 1249; Brandenburg losses of 1296 and 1297 with the Międzyrzecz cells removed; 1300 recorded as a loss to kingdom-of-bohemia), Masovia 5 (1229/1232 Kraków region and keyframes; 1173 region; 1241/1243 gain and loss of Kraków replacing the contests; Dobrzyń Land out from 1248 and the 1332 loss deleted; Kuyavia reading shared). Thin items done: Santok and Wieluń previous holders, Radom mirrored, Bolesław II added to the rulers, dissolve note on 1305-1314.

Differences from the review: (a) 1239-1242 is drawn as Ujście and Nakło, not nothing (note tells the colour agent to drop the keyframe if it prefers nothing); (b) the Wałcz cells are kept in Greater Poland until 1295 because Cliopatria's 1294 shape does not hold them (they left in the 1272 Neumark step) and a 1296 loss of land already lost would be inconsistent; (c) all ten Seniorate events, not only the four named, subtract the Kuyavia cells; (d) no empty keyframe for 1300-1304 (an empty region warns); identity.end stays 1304.

Cross-dossier items other batches own: Brandenburg ledger 3 (1272 gain of 35 cells) overlaps Greater Poland's Wałcz cells until 1295; Silesia has no 1247 Santok loss and its 1232 Kraków gain names duchy-of-greater-poland where this batch has Konrad of Masovia; Bohemia ledger 10 returns the land in 1306 to a dossier that ended in 1304; Sandomierz and Duchies of Poland draw the Wieluń cells that Greater Poland now draws 1249-1299; the Kuyavia dossier (not yet on the mount) will draw Cliopatria's Kuyavia row 1188-1205 while Greater Poland draws it 1186-1198 and Masovia from 1205.
The Dobrzyń Land capture year 1248 is the infobox's ('Duke of Dobrzyń after 1248') plus 'early 1248' for Bolesław I's death; the Casimir I page body gives no year for the capture itself (c2).
